name: Balsaminaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Impatiens capensis through translucent succulent stems, orange zygomorphic spurred flowers, fused stamen/anther cap over the gynoecium and explosively dehiscent 5-valved capsules.

project_scope.note: Impatiens capensis is accepted by current Kew and its native range includes Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the hanging flower and fruit. The project plant is a semi-succulent annual with translucent stems, strongly bilateral flowers with a recurved nectar spur, and touch-sensitive explosive capsules.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual wetland herb with fleshy translucent stems; leaves alternate, ovate-elliptic and coarsely/shallowly serrate.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Showy zygomorphic flowers; sepals and petals highly modified, one sepal forming the sac/spur. Five stamens are connate around/over the gynoecium, forming an anther cap.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Fleshy 5-valved loculicidal capsule that explosively coils its valves and flings seeds when mature.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Translucent succulent stem + orange spurred asymmetric flower + explosive touch-me-not capsule = Balsaminaceae/Impatiens.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: translucent stem → flower orientation → nectar spur → fused stamen cap → capsule before/after touch → cleistogamous flower → wetland habit
visual_lesson.intro: Jewelweed is almost designed for a visual learner: the flower has an obvious nectar spur, and the mature fruit literally demonstrates its dispersal mechanism when touched.

steps.title: 1 · Notice the glassy stem
steps.look_for: Fleshy semi-translucent green stem with swollen nodes.
steps.why_it_matters: Fast vegetative clue in wet habitats.

steps.title: 2 · Find the recurved nectar spur
steps.look_for: Orange-yellow hanging flower with reddish spots and a curved spur bent forward beneath the floral sac.

steps.title: 3 · Decode the irregular petals and sepals
steps.look_for: One sepal expanded into the spurred sac; petals forming upper/lower/lateral portions of the zygomorphic flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents treating every visible lobe as an ordinary petal.

steps.title: 4 · Find the stamen cap
steps.look_for: Five stamens/anthers united into a cap around/over the gynoecium.

steps.title: 5 · Catch the capsule exploding
steps.look_for: Mature elongated capsule splits into five valves that curl rapidly and eject the seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the common name touch-me-not unforgettable.

steps.title: 6 · Show the hidden selfing flowers
steps.look_for: Small closed cleistogamous flowers that can self-fertilize and form capsules later in the season.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds a surprising reproductive strategy without confusing it with the showy flowers.

comparisons.title: Balsaminaceae vs other wetland herbs
comparisons.rule: The combination of translucent succulent stem, spurred bilateral flower and explosive 5-valved capsule is much more diagnostic than wet habitat alone.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not identify jewelweed only from an orange flower. The recurved spur, anther cap and explosive capsule are the transferable family characters.

genera.fast_cue: translucent succulent annual + orange spurred zygomorphic flower + explosive capsule

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range includes Texas.
